mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 15% in the same month indicates weakening consumer and housing demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 15%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates contraction in manufacturing output and signals negative earnings revisions for cyclicals, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points, combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 3%, signals aggressive monetary tightening and heightened inflation risk, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change > 0.75% AND CPIAUCSL > previous month + 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 300,000 alongside a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate below 4% signals an overheating labor market, which raises wage inflation and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent quarterly increase in real GDP (GDPC1) of at least 2% for three consecutive quarters signals a robust economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 2% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 2% AND HOUST < previous month - 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months.
